newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel Corp posts first-quarter loss.
newsitem.headline: Israel Corp posts first-quarter loss.

text.p: Israel Corp, a holding company, reported on Sunday a loss of 35.8 million shekels, or 6.41 shekels a share, in the first quarter.

The company attributed the loss to its Zim Navigation and Oil Refineries Ltd subsidiaries, which posted combined attributable losses to Israel Corp of 44.6 million shekels, compared with profits of 10.6 million shekels a year earlier.

The company, which has holdings in shipping, energy, chemicals, property and high technology, also noted that first-quarter 1996 earnings had been boosted by 23.2 million shekels in capital gains from the sale of a group company. First-quarter 1997 capital gains came to 1.4 million shekels.

Israel Corp had net earnings of 40.3 million shekels, or 7.21 shekels a share, in the year-earlier period. The company slipped into the red in the second half of last year, cutting full-year net to 23.6 million shekels, or 4.23 shekels.
The losses at Zim and Oil Refineries were partly offset by improved results at Israel Chemicals Ltd, which posted a 24.9 percent increase in earnings in the first quarter to 71.6 million shekels.

Israel Corp increased its holding in Israel Chemicals to 41.6 percent from 17 percent during the first quarter but the acquisition will not be reflected in its results until the second quarter, the company said.
Income fell to 781.2 million shekes from 979.5 million shekels a year earlier.
Israel Corp's controlling shareholder Shoul Eisenberg died in March. The heirs, who include the company's new chairman Erwin Eisenberg, have been disputing the terms of his will.
